resources.string: Smallest and lightest on the battery, on the phone\'s hardware encoder when it has one. Lossy: a little of the sound is let go.
Lossless, about 350–450 MB an hour, encoded on the CPU as it records
Lossless; nothing is encoded while recording, the compressing runs after Stop
The plainest: cheapest to encode and to play back, and the best sound at 64 kbps and up.
Rebuilds the high notes from a little data: sounds better than LC below about 48 kbps.
HE with stereo folded into a mono stream: the smallest stereo. Stereo only.
Speech models listen at 16 kHz. Higher keeps more of the room for listening back. HE needs 24 or 48.
Mono is half the encoding for the same bitrate; transcription hears mono either way.
Runs on %1$s, the phone\'s audio hardware
Runs on %1$s, in software on the CPU
This phone has no hardware AAC encoder: Android\'s software one runs, a small share of one CPU core.
Lossy and small, the lightest on the battery: on the phone\'s hardware encoder when it has one.
Lossless: every bit of the sound kept, about 350–450 MB an hour.
Uncompressed: the largest, about 690 MB an hour, with nothing to encode.
